name: Furniture Decoded
background: Founded 1994 by Frank Delgado, who got his nickname flipping competitors' chairs upside down at trade shows to see how they were built — 'decoding furniture' — until the name stuck to the company. Today: ~340 people, one plant and warehouse on Godfrey Ave, three product lines (Fairview task chairs — the flagship, Merritt desks, Stackline shelving). Raw materials: steel tube, plywood and veneer, seat foam, upholstery fabric, fasteners and castors — some imported, most domestic. Eighteen months ago the company rolled out CoreLine ERP, and the building has not fully forgiven it. See docs/company-bible.md for the full bible: voices, running gags, the friction map, and writer rules.

characters.name: Frank Delgado
characters.persona: 58. Built the company from a two-man workshop; decides from the gut and distrusts dashboards. Warm, stubborn, fiercely loyal to the floor. Speech: short declaratives, workshop metaphors, and the running gag — 'In 1994 we did this with a fax machine.'

characters.name: Priya Raman
characters.persona: 41. The calm center and the learner's guide; sees the whole chain when everyone else sees their corner. Dry humor, surgically precise questions, keeps a private 'told-you-so' notebook she never quotes from — people just know it exists. Flaw: absorbs too much herself before delegating.

characters.name: Dale Kowalski
characters.persona: 52, 'Big D'. Knows every rack and pallet from memory and is usually right; trusts his clipboard over CoreLine — 'the computer lies.' Heart of gold, voice like a forklift. Flaw: hides problems to protect his crew until they're too big to hide.

characters.name: Marcus Chen
characters.persona: 29. Fresh certification, earnest to a fault, believes the system is always right and the floor is a rounding error. Ends sentences with '…according to the system.' Flaw: trusts data over eyes. His slow-burn friendship-feud with Dale is the engine of the series.

characters.name: Sofia Marchetti
characters.persona: 45. Charming, relentless, beloved by customers and feared by planners; promises delivery dates first and checks stock second. Signature entrance: 'Small thing — I may have already told the client yes.' Flaw: optimism as a business model.

characters.name: Ray Okafor
characters.persona: 38. Negotiator with three phones and a vendor-gossip network better than any market report. Genuinely good at his job. Flaw: loves a discount slightly more than he loves the risk register — a bargain makes his eyes shine. Sparring partner: Nadia, over payment terms, forever.

characters.name: Nadia Volkov
characters.persona: 49. Nothing gets paid without three matching documents; deadpan delivery, unbeatable memory for invoice numbers. Stamps documents with visible pleasure — the whole floor knows the sound. Flaw: rigid at exactly the wrong moments. Motto: 'The documents agree, or the money stays.'

characters.name: Tommy Nguyen
characters.persona: 22. First job, boundless enthusiasm, asks the 'dumb' question that is secretly the lesson. Flaw: touches things he shouldn't — several stories begin with 'so Tommy pressed a button.' The learner's stand-in and the cast's shared little brother.
